Record Q3: revenue +54% to $16.6M driven by North America +92% on new national accounts (Target, CVS, Wawa).
Heavy China investment ($5.1M quarter, $8.1M YTD) drove adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.9M; management framed spend as front-loaded launch-year anomaly.
China modern-trade rollout via Qifeng expanded into 45+ cities, 33,000 locations, 15,000 key accounts; Asia revenue +273% (partial-quarter contribution).
Europe revenue fell ~50% as Swedish distributor normalized inventory and cycled flavor launches (9M Europe -23%).
Gross margin compressed to 41.5% on promotional allowances, slotting charges, higher production/repackaging costs.
Growth is organic and volume-led; premium pricing maintained, no discounting.
Emerging vending channel (5,000+ machines added) and military channel (60,000+ units/week) seen as key growth channels; vending strategy being replicated in Nordics and China.
Co-packer availability challenging amid sleek-can industry growth; 4 active plus 4 more in talks for 2019; can supply insulated by strong manufacturer relationship.
Production normalized after Q2 bottlenecks; inventory being rebuilt to normalized levels.
Matt Kahn added as EVP of Marketing - no drastic strategy changes, building on existing foundation.
Exploring China strategic partnerships with local retail/advertising investors to accelerate penetration.
Management declined to disclose China same-store sales data when challenged on ~$60/location implied productivity.
Management tone confident and growth-oriented; positioning Celsius as global beverage leader for active health-minded consumers.
Domestic sell-through and Target/CVS door count
More detail on domestic sell-through trends, CVS and Target rollout, and how door count might evolve.

Strong sell-through across channels. Target expanded from ~500-store test to 1,000+ stores with room to scale in 2019; CVS in ~550 locations and growing, positive year-end reviews, active discussions with other drug-channel banners.
Early thoughts on how marketing plans might evolve following new marketing talent.

New EVP Matt Kahn (20+ years' experience) a strong addition but no drastic changes; building on existing foundation with more consumer/trade activation in 2019, staying true to 'live, work and play' core.
How co-packer setup is evolving given increased volumes and how it benefits the company.

Co-packer availability challenging amid sleek-can industry growth; 4 active, 4 more in talks for 2019. Inventory being rebuilt. Industry can-supply concerns but Celsius insulated by strong manufacturer relationship.
More detail on strategic partners being evaluated in China and what areas.
Looking to leverage strategic networks from last two financing rounds (China-based investors); in discussions with additional retail/advertising strategic investors but no further detail to share.
Whether early vending channel success could be replicated in China.

Same vending strategy being replicated in North America, Nordics, and China; healthy vending and office micro-markets a success. China rollout began Q2, successful in Q3, similar opportunities in Hong Kong; partnered with Vistar, Canteen.
How distributors determine which products to place in vending machines - geography or demand.

Standard planograms set up but variances appear based on operator; all flavors available but slot count limited, so marketplace shows variance, core flavors (Kiwi Guava, raspberry/acai, orange) emphasized.
What pricing trends versus prior year/quarter, given mention of premium pricing.
Maintaining pricing, driving strong revenue growth and gross margins without discounting; growth is organic from consumers and reorders, not discount-driven - sustained growth.
How much more money going into China launch, given S&M expense exceeded expectations - was it mostly China?
Confirmed China investment was higher than analysts anticipated, driven by heavy activation tied to entering planograms and retailer resets for 2019.
China investment quantification and anomaly status
Specific China investment figure for the quarter vs YTD, and whether the elevated spend was an anomaly.
YTD China investment ~$8.1M, quarterly ~$5.1M spanning S&M plus other investments. CEO confirmed the elevated quarter was an anomaly, not a go-forward expectation.
7-Eleven update, Nordic inventory, SKU reset timing
Update on 7-Eleven; whether Norway timing/inventory issues resolved; when retailer resets allow more SKUs into Target/CVS.

7-Eleven doing extremely well with good churns via McLane, enabling expansion into Wawa, RaceTrac, QT, Circle K. Nordic inventory normalized, product still growing in-market. Planogram resets typically back half of Q1 into Q2.
Offered congratulatory comments praising the $16.6M revenue milestone, China investment, and Matt Kahn hire.
Management thanked the caller and credited the dedicated team.
China per-location productivity and future revenue
Calculated implied ~$60 product per location ($1.4M Asia revenue / ~25,000 locations); asked if above/below target and why continued China investment drives future revenue growth.

Declined to release same-store sales data; many stores onboarded late in quarter. Footprint ~25,000 through quarter plus additional accounts closed in back half; ~127 sub-distributors and ~15,000 key accounts. Investment to normalize through Q4 and 2019.
